data.title: AI Application Basics
data.tagline: A product that uses an AI model, an interface, and sometimes tools to help people complete tasks
data.learningOutcome: You can explain what the model, tool, and application each do when an assistant checks a calendar.
data.description: When you ask a calendar assistant about tomorrow afternoon, the interface receives the question, the model decides what to look up, a calendar tool reads the real schedule, and the app shows the result. The model does not enter the calendar on its own.

learning.assumes: You have used a chat product that gives continuing answers or shows that it is working.
learning.outcome: You can explain what the model, tool, and application each do when an assistant checks a calendar.

explanation.title: The app describes the tool
explanation.text: It supplies the calendar tool’s allowed parameters, permissions, and the current question.

explanation.title: The model requests an action
explanation.text: It returns a structured request to call the right tool; that is not a calendar result yet.

explanation.title: The app returns a real result
explanation.text: It validates the request, queries the calendar, and gives the result back for a response.

data.boundary: The model generates output, the application handles the flow and permissions, and the tool connects to outside data or actions.

lessonPractice.title: A calendar assistant says there are two meetings tomorrow afternoon, but the product has no calendar permission and made no calendar call. How should this be fixed?

options.label: Have the app request permission, call the calendar tool, and give real results to the AI for wording
options.feedback: AI answers from supplied context and tool results; private schedules require a controlled product capability.

options.label: Let the model infer meetings from the user's tone without connecting a real calendar
options.feedback: A language model cannot know private data without access, so inference turns invented information into a claimed result.

options.label: Write You must query the calendar in the prompt and treat the response as executed
options.feedback: A prompt creates neither tools nor permission; actual execution requires an application call record.

data.agentPrompt: Confirm user permission and an available calendar tool, then query tomorrow afternoon before answering. If permission is missing or the call fails, say the schedule cannot be read and do not guess; preserve time, title, and source.
